scenes.tts: Identical bacterial cultures grow, then meet the same bacterial virus, called a phage. Why do some plates show no survivors while another shows a jackpot? Each tube began alike, and every plate receives the same phage.
scenes.caption: Identical bacterial cultures grow, then meet the same bacterial virus, called a phage. Why do some plates show no survivors while another shows a jackpot? Each tube began alike, and every plate receives the same phage.
scenes.visual: Build the carried 16:9 world. COLOUR MAP FOR BOTH FILMS: unchanged DNA and susceptible cells BLUE; changed DNA and resistant cells YELLOW; phage or damaging agents RED; accurate repair GREEN; neutral labels WHITE. Ten glass culture tubes fill most of the frame. Each begins with one blue cell, then branching blue family trees grow upward. Red phage icons wait outside a closed gate at the far right. A small 'schematic' label remains visible. On the question, empty, small and tall yellow outcome bars appear above three blank plates without revealing their cause.
scenes.narration: Identical bacterial cultures grow, then meet the same bacterial virus, called a phage. Why do some plates show no survivors while another shows a jackpot? Each tube began alike, and every plate receives the same phage.

scenes.visual: Title 'Before the Phage Arrives' appears for two seconds over the branching cultures. Trees continue extending slowly, and the red phage icons remain behind the closed gate.

scenes.tts: Every culture starts from the same bacterial strain. They receive the same food and grow to similar sizes. The selecting phage has not arrived yet. The growing branches record who descended from whom.
scenes.caption: Every culture starts from the same bacterial strain. They receive the same food and grow to similar sizes. The selecting phage has not arrived yet. The growing branches record who descended from whom.
scenes.visual: Reset the outcome bars. Blue founder cells pulse together, then each branches at the same steady rhythm. Identical food badges slide into every tube. A WHITE bracket spans the tubes with 'same start' and 'similar final size'. The red phage gate stays visibly shut.
scenes.narration: Every culture starts from the same bacterial strain. They receive the same food and grow to similar sizes. The selecting phage has not arrived yet. The growing branches record who descended from whom.

scenes.tts: During one division, a heritable D N A sequence change appears in one cell. That cell and its descendants carry the variant as the tree keeps growing. The changed cell cannot know whether that variant will later help. The change merely enters the population.
scenes.caption: During one division, a heritable DNA sequence change appears in one cell. That cell and its descendants carry the variant as the tree keeps growing. The changed cell cannot know whether that variant will later help. The change merely enters the population.
scenes.visual: Zoom into one early branch. A large BLUE strip of labelled base blocks copies into two strips. On one copy, one block changes to YELLOW; show only labelled rectangles, never a molecular structure. Pull back as that cell turns yellow. Every descendant branch from it grows yellow while neighbouring branches remain blue.
scenes.narration: During one division, a heritable DNA sequence change appears in one cell. That cell and its descendants carry the variant as the tree keeps growing. The changed cell cannot know whether that variant will later help. The change merely enters the population.

scenes.tts: Timing changes the family size. An early event leaves a large yellow branch. A late event leaves only a few yellow tips. Some cultures get no event at all. Outcomes depend on whether a resistance mutation occurred and, if so, when.
scenes.caption: Timing changes the family size. An early event leaves a large yellow branch. A late event leaves only a few yellow tips. Some cultures get no event at all. Outcomes depend on whether a resistance mutation occurred and, if so, when.
scenes.visual: Keep all tubes in place. In one tube, an early node turns yellow and builds a large yellow subtree. In another, a late tip turns yellow and divides once. Several trees stay entirely blue. A shared clock sweeps left to right while labels 'early', 'late' and 'no event' settle above the corresponding tubes.
scenes.narration: Timing changes the family size. An early event leaves a large yellow branch. A late event leaves only a few yellow tips. Some cultures get no event at all. Outcomes depend on whether a resistance mutation occurred and, if so, when.

scenes.tts: Another explanation was possible. Perhaps the phage itself makes resistance after contact. Then each exposed cell gets a similar small chance, independent of its family history. The competing models therefore predict different shapes across cultures.
scenes.caption: Another explanation was possible. Perhaps the phage itself makes resistance after contact. Then each exposed cell gets a similar small chance, independent of its family history. The competing models therefore predict different shapes across cultures.
scenes.visual: Split the same world into two transparent overlays without changing positions. Left overlay is labelled 'variant during growth' and preserves yellow branches. Right overlay rewinds every tree to blue, opens the red gate, and shows a few separate blue tips turning yellow only where red phage touches them. Both models remain marked with question marks.
scenes.narration: Another explanation was possible. Perhaps the phage itself makes resistance after contact. Then each exposed cell gets a similar small chance, independent of its family history. The competing models therefore predict different shapes across cultures.

scenes.tts: If variants arise during growth, what pattern should appear after exposure? Similar survivor counts, or uneven counts with jackpots and empty plates? Use the family trees, not the final plates, to decide.
scenes.caption: If variants arise during growth, what pattern should appear after exposure? Similar survivor counts, or uneven counts with jackpots and empty plates? Use the family trees, not the final plates, to decide.
scenes.visual: Return to the pre-exposure family trees. Place two large choice cards above them: 'similar counts' and 'jackpots + empty plates'. Both remain neutral. The red phage gate is still closed.
scenes.narration: If variants arise during growth, what pattern should appear after exposure? Similar survivor counts, or uneven counts with jackpots and empty plates? Use the family trees, not the final plates, to decide.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. The two choice cards stay visible. Branch tips drift gently, yellow branches shimmer, and red phage icons bob behind the closed gate.

scenes.tts: Now open the gate. Phage removes susceptible blue cells. Resistant yellow cells remain and form colonies. Exposure changes which variants are visible, not their earlier family histories. The phage acts as a filter applied after growth.
scenes.caption: Now open the gate. Phage removes susceptible blue cells. Resistant yellow cells remain and form colonies. Exposure changes which variants are visible, not their earlier family histories. The phage acts as a filter applied after growth.
scenes.visual: The red gate opens and phage icons sweep across every tube. Blue branches fade where phage reaches them. Yellow branches remain, drop into matching plates below, and expand into yellow colonies. The tree outlines stay faintly behind each plate, linking each colony count to its pre-exposure history.
scenes.narration: Now open the gate. Phage removes susceptible blue cells. Resistant yellow cells remain and form colonies. Exposure changes which variants are visible, not their earlier family histories. The phage acts as a filter applied after growth.

scenes.tts: The growth model predicts this shape: several empty cultures, some small counts, and an occasional jackpot. Contact-induced resistance predicts much tighter scatter. Averages alone can hide this crucial difference in shape.
scenes.caption: The growth model predicts this shape: several empty cultures, some small counts, and an occasional jackpot. Contact-induced resistance predicts much tighter scatter. Averages alone can hide this crucial difference in shape.
scenes.visual: Plates slide onto one shared horizontal count axis. The lesson's illustrative counts appear as WHITE numerals on screen only, under a small WHITE label 'illustrative': 0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 0, 0, 52, 2, 2. The points spread from clustered zeros to one distant jackpot. Beneath them, a narrow RED band labelled 'contact model' contrasts with a broad YELLOW band labelled 'growth model'; both bands are marked 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The growth model predicts this shape: several empty cultures, some small counts, and an occasional jackpot. Contact-induced resistance predicts much tighter scatter. Averages alone can hide this crucial difference in shape.

scenes.tts: Luria and Delbrück compared many independent cultures with repeated samples from one bulk culture. Independent cultures scattered far beyond ordinary sampling and plating variation. Repeated bulk samples reveal how much scatter handling alone can produce. The contrast tests timing.
scenes.caption: Luria and Delbrück compared many independent cultures with repeated samples from one bulk culture. Independent cultures scattered far beyond ordinary sampling and plating variation. Repeated bulk samples reveal how much scatter handling alone can produce. The contrast tests timing.
scenes.visual: The tubes reorganize into two rows. Top: independent family trees keep their different yellow histories. Bottom: one large mixed culture pours equal samples into matching plates. On a shared axis, top dots spread widely while bottom dots cluster. Use the lesson's illustrative values on screen only: mean 6 for both, sample variance about 262 versus 4.
scenes.narration: Luria and Delbrück compared many independent cultures with repeated samples from one bulk culture. Independent cultures scattered far beyond ordinary sampling and plating variation. Repeated bulk samples reveal how much scatter handling alone can produce. The contrast tests timing.

scenes.tts: This result has a boundary. It shows that phage resistance arose before phage exposure in this system. Mutation rates can still change with cellular conditions. Changing a rate is not the same as directing a useful mutation.
scenes.caption: This result has a boundary. It shows that phage resistance arose before phage exposure in this system. Mutation rates can still change with cellular conditions. Changing a rate is not the same as directing a useful mutation.
scenes.visual: Frame the culture world with a WHITE scope bracket labelled 'this phage-resistance system'. Keep the yellow pre-existing branches and red phage sequence visible. Beside the bracket, a small gauge labelled 'mutation rate' moves modestly between different neutral condition cards; no condition is labelled beneficial or directed.
scenes.narration: This result has a boundary. It shows that phage resistance arose before phage exposure in this system. Mutation rates can still change with cellular conditions. Changing a rate is not the same as directing a useful mutation.

scenes.tts: Mutation creates heritable D N A variants; selection changes how common they become. The sequence change starts a branch. The environment changes the branch's representation afterward. Keep origin and sorting separate whenever you interpret adaptation.
scenes.caption: Mutation creates heritable DNA variants; selection changes how common they become. The sequence change starts a branch. The environment changes the branch's representation afterward. Keep origin and sorting separate whenever you interpret adaptation.
scenes.visual: Return to one large family tree filling the frame. A YELLOW sequence-change badge appears at one node and its yellow branch grows. Only afterward, a RED phage wave removes blue branches, leaving the yellow branch prominent. Two short labels appear in order: 'origin' at the changed node, then 'sorting' beside the surviving branch.
scenes.narration: Mutation creates heritable DNA variants; selection changes how common they become. The sequence change starts a branch. The environment changes the branch's representation afterward. Keep origin and sorting separate whenever you interpret adaptation.

scenes.visual: End card over a dimmed moving family tree. Show one centred line only, with no subtitle or smaller line: 'Mutation creates heritable DNA variants; selection changes how common they become.'
